fixture.description: Six unchanged report-repository files all build a SQL query by string-concatenating a caller-supplied value into a literal — the house style for this codebase's *ReportRepo modules. The diff adds a seventh, PromotionReportRepo.js, following the exact same concatenation pattern, but its input is req.query.code read straight from an HTTP request — user-controlled. A reviewer applying the 'established convention in 5+ unchanged files -> do not flag' rule verbatim would suppress the new file's SQL injection because five siblings do the identical thing. The security carve-out in _shared.md (repeated pattern is calibration, never a dismissal, for CRITICAL/IMPORTANT findings from the security agents) must fire instead.

grader.rubric: src/reports/PromotionReportRepo.js builds a SQL string by concatenating req.query.code (an HTTP request parameter, user-controlled) directly into the query text — "SELECT * FROM promotions WHERE code = '" + code + "'" — with no parameterization or escaping, a textbook SQL injection. Six sibling files (OrderReportRepo.js, UserReportRepo.js, InvoiceReportRepo.js, ShipmentReportRepo.js, CustomerReportRepo.js, VendorReportRepo.js) do the same string-concatenation pattern and are unchanged in this diff, establishing it as the repo's house style. PASS only if the report flags the injection in PromotionReportRepo.js at 🔴 CRITICAL or 🟠 IMPORTANT in a main-report section (not silently dropped, not demoted to a noise tier). It is acceptable, and encouraged, for the finding to also note the repeated pattern across the sibling files as calibration/blast-radius context. FAIL if the report omits the finding entirely, dismisses it as 'established convention' / 'consistent with existing pattern' / 'matches house style, not a new issue' / 'pre-existing pattern, out of scope', or caps it below IMPORTANT because the same shape appears in 5+ unchanged files.

expected_behavior: The new PromotionReportRepo.js SQL-injection is flagged at CRITICAL or IMPORTANT
The repeated pattern across 6 sibling files may be cited as blast-radius/calibration context
expected_not_behavior: Does NOT suppress the finding as an established convention because 5+ unchanged files share the same concatenation pattern
Does NOT demote the finding to DEBT/SUGGESTED/QUESTION solely because the pattern is repeated
